findings.title: describe(reduce='TSNE') crashes with default max_dims (documented model unusable in describe)
findings.description: describe()'s docstring explicitly lists TSNE among supported reduce models, but its summary loop calls reduce for every dims in range(2, max_dims). sklearn TSNE only allows n_components < 4 with the default barnes_hut method, so on any data with >= 5 features (max_dims >= 5) the loop crashes at dims=4 with a raw sklearn ValueError. Even capping max_dims=4 only works when n_samples > 30 (default perplexity, see -002). The same applies to any model with an upper n_components bound. describe should either clamp/skip infeasible dims, switch TSNE to method='exact', or document that TSNE requires max_dims <= 4.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x = np.random.default_rng(3).normal(size=(50, 15)); hyp.describe(x, reduce='TSNE', show=False)"
findings.expected: A correlation-by-components result for TSNE (docstring: 'Models supported: ... TSNE ...'), or a clear hypertools error saying TSNE only supports up to 3 components in describe.
findings.actual: ValueError: 'n_components' should be inferior to 4 for the barnes_hut algorithm as it relies on quad-tree or oct-tree.

findings.title: reduce(x, 'TSNE') crashes on datasets with <= 30 rows (sklearn default perplexity passed through)
findings.description: sklearn TSNE's default perplexity=30 requires n_samples > 30. hyp.reduce passes the default through, so TSNE on any dataset of 30 or fewer rows (common in psychology/neuro pilot data) crashes with an error about a parameter the user never set. The fix (dict spec {'model':'TSNE','kwargs':{'perplexity':...}}) is discoverable but hypertools could clamp perplexity to min(30, n_samples-1) or append a hint. Upstream-inherent, so filed minor rather than critical.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.default_rng(2).normal(size=(30, 8)), 'TSNE', ndims=2)"
findings.expected: A 2D TSNE embedding, or a hypertools-level message explaining how to lower perplexity via the dict spec.
findings.actual: ValueError: perplexity (30.0) must be less than n_samples (30)

findings.title: reduce docstring 'If the input is a list, a list is returned' is false for single-element lists
findings.description: reduce() unwraps single-dataset results unless internal=True: hyp.reduce([a], 'PCA', ndims=3) returns a bare ndarray, not a 1-element list. The Returns section states 'If the input is a list, a list is returned.' Code behavior is intentional (plot-pipeline convenience) so the docstring should be corrected (list returned only when input has >1 dataset, or when internal=True). Also: 'x : Numpy array or list of arrays' omits DataFrames/text even though format_data (and the code, verified) accepts DataFrames, lists of DataFrames, mixed lists, and lists of strings - describe's docstring does mention DataFrames.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.reduce([np.random.rand(40, 12)], 'PCA', ndims=3); print(type(r))"
findings.expected: <class 'list'> per the docstring (or a corrected docstring).

findings.title: ndims=None (the default) and ndims >= n_features silently return the input unchanged - no reduction, no warning
findings.description: hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA') with the default ndims=None, and hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA', ndims=k) with k >= n_features, both hit the early return 'if model_params['n_components'] is None or all([i.shape[1] <= n_components ...])' and hand back the (formatted) input verbatim - verified np.array_equal(result, x) == True for ndims == n_features. A scientist requesting PCA at full dimensionality reasonably expects the variance-ordered rotation (sklearn PCA(n_components=8) on 8 features rotates; hypertools returns raw data). Neither behavior is documented ('ndims : int, Number of dimensions to reduce' says nothing about None or the skip). Legacy-compatible, but for 1.0 at minimum the docstring should state it and ideally a warning should fire when a named model is silently skipped.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x = np.random.default_rng(2).normal(size=(30, 8)); print(hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA').shape); print(np.array_equal(hyp.reduce(x, 'PCA', ndims=8), x))"
findings.expected: Documented behavior; ideally a UserWarning that the reduction was skipped, or the actual PCA rotation when the user explicitly named a model.
findings.actual: (30, 8) and True - input returned verbatim with no warning.

findings.title: Invalid reduce= spec error: never names the offending value, contains run-on whitespace, and links to hypertools 0.8 docs
findings.description: Misspelled strings ('PCa', lowercase 'umap'), reduce=42, objects missing fit_transform/n_components, and unfitted Reducer wrappers all raise the same ValueError. findings.title: Canonical dict-spec error message instructs users to use the DEPRECATED 'params' key
findings.description: Passing the canonical 1.0 dict form without a 'model' key (e.g. {'kwargs': {'whiten': True}}) raises: 'If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the "model" key and a dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key.' - but 'params' is the legacy spec that itself emits a DeprecationWarning; the canonical spec uses 'args'/'kwargs'. Following the error's advice produces deprecated code. Both raise sites (reduce.py lines 166 and 201) share the outdated text.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(30, 8), {'kwargs': {'whiten': True}}, ndims=3)"

findings.actual: ValueError: If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the "model" key and a                 dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key.

findings.title: Ragged dataset lists (unequal column counts) fail with a raw numpy vstack error
findings.description: hyp.reduce([x_30x8, y_30x5], 'PCA', ndims=3) (and mixed 2D+1D lists) dies inside np.vstack with numpy's concatenation error. Nothing tells the user that hypertools reduces lists in a SHARED space and therefore requires equal feature counts, nor points to align/padding options. format_data passes ragged numeric lists through untouched, so the crash surfaces from deep inside reduce_list.

findings.title: Fitted-Reducer reuse crashes with raw AttributeError for TSNE/MDS/SpectralEmbedding (models without .transform)
findings.description: The docstring promises: 'A previously-fitted Reducer (as returned by return_model=True) is applied via .transform instead of being refit.' sklearn's TSNE, MDS and SpectralEmbedding have no transform method, so reusing their fitted Reducer on new data raises AttributeError: 'TSNE' object has no attribute 'transform' from inside Reducer.transform. No caveat in the docstring and no friendly error ('TSNE cannot transform new data; refit instead').
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; rng = np.random.default_rng(2); _, m = hyp.reduce(rng.normal(size=(40, 8)), 'TSNE', ndims=2, return_model=True, random_state=0); hyp.reduce(rng.normal(size=(5, 8)), reduce=m)"
findings.expected: A hypertools error naming the limitation and the fix, e.g. 'fitted TSNE models cannot embed new data; call reduce() on the combined data instead' - plus a docstring caveat.
findings.actual: AttributeError: 'TSNE' object has no attribute 'transform'  (same for 'MDS' and 'SpectralEmbedding')

findings.title: describe() docs say it correlates 'covariance'; it actually correlates pairwise Euclidean DISTANCE matrices (and the summary line is ungrammatical)
findings.description: describe.py's first docstring line reads 'Create plot describing covariance with as a function of number of dimensions' (broken grammar), and examples/plot_describe.py says it 'computes the covariance (samples by samples) of both the raw and reduced datasets'. The implementation (get_cdist) uses scipy.spatial.distance.cdist(x, x) - Euclidean distance matrices, not covariance - then Pearson-correlates the flattened matrices (verified by exact independent recomputation, max diff 0.0). Docs should say 'pairwise-distance (or similarity) structure', not covariance.
findings.repro: grep -n 'covariance' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/reduce/describe.py /Users/jmanning/hypertools/examples/plot_describe.py; env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import inspect; from hypertools.reduce import describe as d; import hypertools.reduce.describe as m; print(inspect.getsource(m.get_cdist))"
findings.expected: Docstring/example text describing correlation of pairwise Euclidean distance matrices.
findings.actual: describe.py:15 'Create plot describing covariance with as a function of number of dimensions'; plot_describe.py:9-11 'computes the covariance (samples by samples)'; code: return cdist(x, x)

findings.title: describe max_dims is an EXCLUSIVE bound: 'Maximum number of dimensions to consider' is off by one
findings.description: summary() iterates 'for dims in range(2, max_dims)', so max_dims=5 evaluates dims 2,3,4 only (verified: len(result['average']) == 3) and the maximum dimensionality actually considered is max_dims-1. The user-facing docstring 'max_dims : int, Maximum number of dimensions to consider' implies inclusive. Either make the loop inclusive (range(2, max_dims+1)) or document the exclusive semantics.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.describe(np.random.rand(50, 15), max_dims=5, show=False); print(len(r['average']))"
findings.expected: 4 values (dims 2..5) per the docstring wording, or a docstring stating the bound is exclusive.

findings.title: Multi-dataset describe figure (matplotlib): indistinguishable same-color unlabeled traces, no legend, and the 'average' curve is never plotted; plotly backend differs
findings.description: With a list input the matplotlib backend draws every individual trace in the same seaborn default blue with alpha=0.7 and no legend (verified on 2-dataset and 3-dataset weights_sample figures: traces cannot be attributed to datasets). The plotly backend names each trace 'dataset i' with a legend, so the two backends disagree visually despite the docstring emphasizing equivalence ('The return value (a dict) is identical either way' - true, but the figures diverge). Additionally the headline result['average'] curve (the number most users act on, and the only one whose length can differ - avg had 13 points vs individual 7 in the unequal-trace test) is not drawn by either backend.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp; rng = np.random.default_rng(3); hyp.describe([rng.normal(size=(9, 15)), rng.normal(size=(9, 15))], show=True); plt.gcf().savefig('/tmp/describe_traces.png')"
findings.expected: Distinguishable per-dataset colors + legend (like the plotly backend), and ideally the average curve overlaid.
findings.actual: Two identical-color unlabeled lines; no legend; no average curve (see evidence PNGs).

findings.title: get_corr is called with its arguments in the opposite order of its parameter names
findings.description: describe.py line 112 calls get_corr(alldims, reduced) but the signature is get_corr(reduced, alldims). Pearson correlation is symmetric so results are unaffected (verified numerically), but the mismatch is a maintenance trap for anyone extending get_corr to an asymmetric measure.
findings.expected: Call-site argument order matching the parameter names.
findings.actual: describe.py:112 'corrs.append(get_corr(alldims, reduced))' vs describe.py:173 'def get_corr(reduced, alldims):'

findings.title: `import hypertools.reduce.reduce as m` fails because the top-level function shadows the subpackage
findings.description: hypertools/__init__.py binds hypertools.reduce to the FUNCTION, shadowing the hypertools.reduce subpackage attribute. As a result 'import hypertools.reduce.reduce as m' raises ImportError: cannot import name 'reduce' from 'reduce' (unknown location) - a confusing message. 'from hypertools.reduce.reduce import reduce' and importlib.import_module both work. Long-standing hypertools convention; worth a docs note for power users who import submodules (e.g. reduce.common.Reducer).
findings.expected: Either a working import or documentation of the supported import forms.
findings.actual: ImportError: cannot import name 'reduce' from 'reduce' (unknown location)

findings.title: describe() gives no handle on its figure (show-only): cannot save, style, or embed it
findings.description: describe returns only the results dict; the matplotlib figure is created internally and plt.show()n, the plotly figure is fig.show()n and discarded. hyp.plot returns the Figure, so describe is the one plotting entry point whose visual cannot be programmatically saved (users must scrape plt.gcf() before it is garbage-collected, which is what this audit had to do). Suggest returning the figure in the dict (e.g. result['fig']) or adding a save/ax parameter.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.describe(np.random.rand(40, 10), show=True); print(sorted(r.keys()))"
findings.expected: Some way to obtain the rendered figure (return value or parameter).
findings.actual: ['average', 'individual'] - no figure reference; matplotlib prints 'FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown' under Agg.

findings.title: Dependency warnings leak through every MDS/UMAP reduce call (sklearn 1.8 FutureWarnings, umap UserWarning)
findings.description: hyp.reduce(x, 'MDS', ...) always emits two sklearn FutureWarnings ('The default value of n_init will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9', 'The default value of init will change from random to classical_mds in 1.10') because hypertools constructs MDS() with library defaults; hypertools controls the constructor and could pass explicit values to keep 1.0 output clean and future-proof (the changing defaults will also silently change MDS results at sklearn 1.9/1.10). UMAP+random_state likewise always warns 'n_jobs value 1 overridden to 1 by setting random_state' and 'Tensorflow not installed; ParametricUMAP will be unavailable' (upstream, harder to control).
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(60, 20), 'MDS', ndims=2, random_state=0)"
findings.expected: No FutureWarnings on default usage (pin n_init/init explicitly), keeping MDS results stable across sklearn upgrades.
findings.actual: FutureWarning: The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9. ... | FutureWarning: The default value of `init` will change from 'random' to 'classical_mds' in 1.10. ...

findings.title: Cross-module normalize= with a wrong value fails with an AssertionError that never names the offending value
findings.description: hyp.reduce(x, reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='zscore') - a natural guess since manip='ZScore' is valid - raises AssertionError: 'scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' Issues: (1) AssertionError instead of ValueError/TypeError (assertions vanish under python -O); (2) the offending value 'zscore' is not echoed; (3) reduce()'s docstring for the cross-module kwargs ('manip, normalize, align, cluster : model spec or None') gives no hint of the accepted normalize values. Root cause lives in the normalize stage but it is reachable through reduce's documented API surface.
findings.repro: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.rand(40, 12), reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='zscore')"
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize='zscore' is not recognized; use 'across', 'within', 'row', 'none', or a fitted Normalizer.
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: [infra/release-hygiene] repo .venv contains a stale non-editable hypertools 1.0.0.dev0 whose reduce() still has the fixed dict-spec/ndims bug
findings.description: Tagged infra. .venv/bin/pip show hypertools -> 1.0.0.dev0 installed as a site-packages COPY, not editable. Running the audit without PYTHONPATH imported that copy, in which (a) reduce lacks the ndims validation and (b) the canonical dict spec ignores ndims: hyp.reduce([a,b], reduce={'model':'PCA','kwargs':{'whiten':True}}, ndims=3) returned FULL-dimensional (40, 12)/(25, 12) - exactly the bug the repo source's QC-2026-07 comment says was fixed (repo source verified correct: (40, 3)/(25, 3)). Any developer, CI job, or other audit unit running .venv/bin/python without PYTHONPATH is testing stale code and could mis-report release status. Reinstall editable (pip install -e) or refresh the install before release sign-off (not performed by this audit: modifying the venv is out of scope).
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/pip show hypertools | head -3 && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp, numpy as np; rng = np.random.default_rng(0); a = rng.normal(size=(40, 12)); b = rng.normal(size=(25, 12)); print([r.shape for r in hyp.reduce([a, b], reduce={'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'whiten': True}}, ndims=3)])"
findings.expected: [(40, 3), (25, 3)] (what the repo source on audit/release-1.0-2026-07 produces).
findings.actual: Version: 1.0.0.dev0 (non-editable); output [(40, 12), (25, 12)] - ndims silently ignored by the stale installed copy; traceback paths point at .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypertools/.
